name: freelance-finance-tracker
summary: Local‑first freelance finance tracker with receipt capture, mileage logging, encrypted on‑device storage, backup/restore, CSV/PDF export and optional app lock. All data stays on the phone; no server, accounts or analytics.
steps: 1. Add the policy text and version to src/lib/policy.ts and make the policy gate store acceptance date/version via the encrypted Store.

2. Extend src/navigation/index.tsx with four bottom‑tab routes: Dashboard, Receipts, Mileage, Settings. Add a stack navigator for modal screens (receipt entry, mileage entry, app‑lock, export, backup/restore).
3. Define core data types (Receipt, MileageEntry, AppSettings) in src/lib/models.ts.
4. Implement a thin domain layer:
• src/lib/finance.ts – functions to sum income/expenses, compute mileage deduction and estimated tax.
• src/lib/receiptStore.ts – typed wrappers around getStore() for CRUD on the "receipts" collection.
• src/lib/mileageStore.ts – wrapper for the "mileage" collection.
• src/lib/mileage.ts – mileage‑deduction calculation based on a per‑mile rate from settings.

5. Build the DashboardScreen using shared UI components (Screen, SummaryCard, ReceiptCard, MileageCard, EmptyState). Show total income, expenses, mileage deduction, tax estimate and a list of the most recent records.
6. Create ReceiptsScreen (list) and ReceiptEntryScreen (form). Use FormField, ChoiceField (expense / income) and PrimaryButton. Persist the record via receiptStore.
7. Add a basic SettingsScreen with navigation links to sub‑screens that will be added later (App Lock, Tax Settings, Export, Backup/Restore).
8. Write shared UI components for receipts and mileage cards (ReceiptCard.tsx, MileageCard.tsx) and a generic ExportButton component.
9. Milestone 2 – Photo capture and mileage logging:
• Add expo-image-picker & expo-file-system usage in src/lib/photoPicker.ts and UI wrapper ReceiptImagePicker.tsx.
• Extend the Receipt model with optional photoUri (already in models) and modify ReceiptEntryScreen to allow attaching a photo.
• Implement MileageScreen (list) and MileageEntryScreen (form) using FormField, PrimaryButton and the mileageStore.
• Create MileageCard UI component.
10. Milestone 3 – Settings, app lock & export:
• Create src/lib/settings.ts – typed getters/setters for mileageRate, taxRate and appLockEnabled (stored in the Store).
• Implement src/lib/appLock.ts – thin wrapper around expo‑local‑authentication that can be called from App.tsx after policy acceptance.
• Modify src/App.tsx to prompt for biometric authentication when appLockEnabled is true.
• Build sub‑screens: AppLockScreen (toggle), TaxSettingsScreen (inputs for mileageRate & taxRate), ExportScreen (buttons to generate CSV & PDF).
• Implement CSV export in src/lib/exportCsv.ts (uses fast‑csv‑like string building) and PDF export in src/lib/exportPdf.ts (uses expo‑print to turn simple HTML into a PDF).
• Wire ExportButton to call the two export helpers and share the file via expo‑sharing.
11. Milestone 4 – Encrypted backup & restore:
• Write src/lib/backup.ts – serialize all collections, encrypt the JSON blob with a key derived from a user‑provided passphrase (scrypt via src/lib/crypto.ts) and output a Base64‑encoded file.
• Build BackupScreen (show a PrimaryButton that asks for a passphrase, creates the encrypted blob and invokes expo‑sharing).
• Build RestoreScreen (prompt for a backup file, ask for the passphrase, decrypt, validate JSON shape, then replace the Store contents via clearAll + bulk put).
• Add UI buttons BackupButton.tsx and RestoreButton.tsx used in the respective screens.
12. Add required Expo dependencies (expo-image-picker, expo-file-system, expo-sharing, expo-print, expo-local-authentication) via npm install –save‑dev or expo install.
13. Write unit tests for all pure‑logic modules (finance, mileage, backup, settings, appLock) and integration tests that exercise the Store with the in‑memory implementation used by the test harness.
14. Run the template’s existing tests to ensure nothing was broken, then run the newly added acceptance tests for each milestone.

milestones.name: M1: Policy gate, core navigation & receipt entry
milestones.goal: User can accept the policy, navigate the tab bar, add an expense receipt (amount, date, category, type, notes) and see a basic dashboard with total income/expenses. Settings screen shows placeholder links.

milestones.name: M2: Photo capture & mileage logging
milestones.goal: User can attach a photo to a receipt, add mileage entries (date, miles, purpose) and view them. Mileage deduction is calculated using the default IRS rate.

milestones.name: M3: Settings, app lock & export
milestones.goal: User can configure mileage & tax rates, enable optional biometric app lock, and generate CSV/PDF tax‑ready reports that can be shared.

milestones.name: M4: Encrypted backup & restore
milestones.goal: User can create an encrypted backup file protected by a passphrase, share it, and later restore the whole app state from such a file with integrity checks and friendly error messages.
